findings.evidence: Proof body `simp only [← mk_trans, eq]; exact ⟨Path.Homotopy.subpathTransSubpath p a b c⟩` uses neither hypothesis; `subpathTransSubpath γ t₀ t₁ t₂` is defined for arbitrary points.
findings.fix: Drop `_hab`/`_hbc`, making it an unconditional simp lemma; correspondingly remove the `part.mono …` arguments passed at the two `rw [← subpath_trans …]` sites in PathHomotopyDiscreteness.lean:444,449.
findings.issue: `Path.Homotopic.Quotient.subpath_trans` takes `_hab : a ≤ b` and `_hbc : b ≤ c`, both unused (underscore-named); the underlying `Path.Homotopy.subpathTransSubpath` (mathlib Topology/Subpath.lean:132) needs no ordering, so the statement holds unconditionally. As a `@[simp]` lemma the extra side goals also hurt applicability.

findings.evidence: `fromPath` is an `abbrev` for the identity arrow (mathlib FundamentalGroup.lean:75); `1` is `𝟙`, equal only by unfolding.
findings.fix: Introduce/apply an explicit `fromPath ⟦Path.refl _⟧ = 1` lemma (or add a comment) at both sites instead of a bare `rfl`.
findings.issue: The `rfl` closing `h_map` (and the analogous `rw [h_map_eq, Quotient.sound hhom]; rfl` at line 93) rests on the undocumented definitional equality `FundamentalGroup.fromPath ⟦Path.refl u⟧ = 1` across the `fromPath`/group-`One` wrappers — the same wrapper defeq the PR otherwise names via `map_fromPath`.

summary: Proofs are mostly robust and well-structured, and the long pasting lemma carries adequate structural comments. Two issues: a simp lemma with redundant order hypotheses, and two rfl steps resting on undocumented wrapper defeq.
